qualification: Twelve authored short VP9/PCM cases verify complete untrimmed samples and exact sourcePTS=originalPTS-CodecDelay. Six fail before: rounded latency/sample origins place a retained sample1ns below zero, ceil discards its nonpadding neighbor. Strict off-grid negatives and positive origins are separate controls.

Zero-origin clipping now uses the nearest count only when its sample time is no earlier than-1ns; that tiny residue clamps to0. Genuine off-grid preroll still ceils. Exact CodecDelay read/index/seek coordinates are unchanged.

Actual workers verify data/PTS through playback, rewind and seek0. Independent owned decoding agrees for zero-origin sample-count cases; full-preroll root EOF is acceptance while owned no-samples export remains a refusal.

Additional synthetic Opus/Vorbis negative-origin acceptance restores the same two-frame trim. Their direct native controls remain finite and frame-exact; Opus is compared to its decoded control rather than incorrectly assuming DTX is bit-zero. These are codec variants of the scalar failure, not additional IDs or conformance claims.

Positive1ns seek retains strict ceil for Opus/Vorbis. CodecDelay overflow reports its specific clock error with no backend PCM. The earlier54 one-ns oracle now preserves its sample; encoded literal timestamp tests remain exact.
Unit/build checks apply to final library source; the final integration rerun corrects only an overstrict DTX-zero test oracle. No public signatures, performance or physical-DAC claim.
compatibility: PCM presentation at a quantized-1ns zero boundary is now retained at0 instead of losing one whole sample. Encoded timestamps remain literal. Off-grid/user seek boundaries keep their prior strict behavior.
counting: One zero-origin sample-grid clipping improvement; metadata fields, rates, codecs, controls and oracle corrections add no IDs.
